investing: A Montana mineral investment should be traced from the recorded interest to the paid decimal before a yield or multiple is trusted. The file identifies the county, legal description, ownership fraction, lease royalty, unit participation, deductions, taxes, producing wells, operator, statement months, and any title assumption still open.

Nearby wells, spacing, permits, operator activity, and a basin label can add context without proving future development. Base, downside, and upside cases need the same ownership fraction and paid decimal.
Stress One Cash Assumption at a Time
Production decline, prices, downtime, deductions, taxes, curtailment, and operator concentration should be tested separately so a title assumption is not hidden inside an economic forecast.

Every material number should keep its source and date. The record should state the holding period, liquidity limits, title expense, tax questions, and the event that would invalidate the original case.
exchange-1031: Potential exchange treatment should be discussed with a qualified intermediary and independent tax counsel before a sale closes or proceeds are received. The file identifies the selling entity, property, expected proceeds, closing date, deadlines, and proposed replacement property.
Keep Record Work and Federal Timing Distinct

Deed work, probate, trust authority, reservations, corrective instruments, and payor records can move on a different schedule from exchange deadlines. Each open item needs a responsible professional and written status.

The sale agreement, deed, legal description, retained-interest language, settlement statement, intermediary instructions, and replacement identification should not quietly change acreage, depth, county, or ownership fraction.

The completed file should retain the agreement, recorded deed, exact description, settlement statement, intermediary instructions, identification notices, replacement documents, title correspondence, and recording information.
